messages:
joel_s: alerts firing across eu-west3 -- autoscaler not adding nodes, a bunch of inference pods Pending. seeing FailedCreate and node events stuck at PROVISIONING. anyone oncall? :eyes:
ops-bot: Incident created: #INC-2026-042 eu-west3 provisioning failures (severity P1). Pager sent to oncall rotation.
chen_w: jumping in, looking at cloud API errors now. I can see repeated 429s to the cloud provisioning API and a handful of `ExceededResourceQuota` entries.
maria_g: from infra logs: `error: quotaExceeded: projects/rdw-prod/regions/eu-west3: insufficient accelerators (GPUs) available for requested instance` -- looks like capacity shortage in the region, not just quota.
tanvi_p: interesting — not a quota increase; cloud is returning "ZONE_RESOURCE_UNAVAILABLE" in some calls. Could be regional capacity pressure or a rolling maintenance.
joel_s: traffic is spiking due to a partner job batch. Autoscaler relies on nodepool provisioning; when it gets the bad signals it backs off and we end up thrashing. we need to stop the thrash and either force capacity or shift traffic.
sre_lead: propose immediate mitigations: 1) enable cross-region fallback (route 30% to eu-west2) 2) add emergency reserved instances in eu-west3 via manual provisioning 3) pause scale-down to keep existing nodes 
chen_w: starting traffic shift. updating routing weight to send 30% to eu-west2 via global router: `curl -X POST https://router.internal/weights -d '{"eu-west2":0.3}'` -- done.
joel_s: seeing reduced pressure on eu-west3 queue, Pending pods dropping by ~40%. Good.
maria_g: manual node provisioning attempt: `gcloud compute instances create rwd-emg-1 --zone=europe-west3-b --machine-type=n1-standard-8 --accelerator=type=nvidia-t4,count=1` repeatedly returns `ZONE_RESOURCE_POOL_EXHAUSTED`. cloud support ticket opened.
tanvi_p: since nodes won't provision, let's scale up Dedicated capacity in eu-west2 and temporarily pin heavy workloads there. This increases cost but keeps latency acceptable.
sre_lead: approved emergency capacity move. @maria_g can you spin up 10 nodes in eu-west2 reserved pool? Expect cost ~ +$2k/day, approved for incident window.
maria_g: on it, launching reserved instances in eu-west2. command: ```
# create reserved pool (internal)
internalctl create-pool --region eu-west2 --name emg-temp --gpu-type t4 --count 10
```
ops-bot: Routing update: 30% -> eu-west2 applied at 1767554680. Autoscaler pause for eu-west3 applied.
chen_w: autoscaler config shows backoff due to repeated 429s; I'll bump scaleUp cooldown to avoid thrash once provisioning resumes. Patch: `kubectl patch cm autoscaler-config -n infra --type merge -p '{"data":{"scaleUpCooldown":"300s"}}'`
joel_s: can we add a transient fallback policy to route traffic away from nodes that report provisioning errors? would be safer than whole-region weight shifts.
sre_lead: yes, file an action for Optimize to add signal-based routing tomorrow. For now the manual weight shift + reserved pool is sufficient.
maria_g: eu-west2 nodes are healthy, pods are landing. Latency for rerouted requests up ~15-30ms but within SLO.
tanvi_p: cost hit acknowledged. Please log expected dollars in the incident ticket.
ops-bot: Incident update: severity downgraded P2 at 1767555300 (traffic shifted + reserved capacity). Postmortem owner: chen_w, due in 72h.
joel_s: short-term checklist: (1) keep autoscaler paused for eu-west3 until cloud confirms capacity stable, (2) maintain eu-west2 reserved pool until next maintenance window, (3) collect kube events + cloud API traces for postmortem.
chen_w: collecting traces now, grabbing `kubectl describe` for stuck pods and cloud API request ids. will post artifacts to the ticket.
maria_g: created emergency billing estimate: `+~$2.2k/day` while reserved pool active. Added to incident doc.
tanvi_p: thanks everyone. after-action: review autoscaler backoff logic and add hysteresis for provisioning errors (dont treat 429/zone_unavailable as normal scale failure).
ops-bot: Incident closed (mitigated) at 1767555432 — monitoring. Reminder: create postmortem and tag eng-infra, eng-runtime, product.
